structuralViolations.clause: §0.6 F21: "`WidgetIntent.capability`, `WidgetIntent.handoff_capability_ref`, `IntentTarget` of class `c`, `IntentRecord.capability`, **`IntentRecord.handoff_capability_ref`**, every row key of `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY`, and every argument of `subjectCapability`, `subjectFloor`, `requiredConfirmationKind`, `SENSITIVE_DEST`, `RUN_OPENING` and `verificationFloor` are typed `CapabilityRef`, never `string`." — against §0.8 F41 `declare function subjectCapability(i: IntentSubject): CapabilityRef | null;` and §0.8 F43 `function verificationFloor(i: FloorSubject, kind: WidgetKind): VerificationLevel`.
structuralViolations.consequence: Two normative clauses that cannot both be satisfied. Neither `subjectCapability` nor `verificationFloor` takes a `CapabilityRef` argument at all: their arguments are `IntentSubject`, `FloorSubject` and `WidgetKind`. F21 is the owning declaration (§0.2's map gives `CapabilityRef` to §0), so read literally it requires retyping `verificationFloor`'s parameters — which destroys F43's derivation, four of whose six declared inputs (`i.effect`, `i.priority`, `i.target`, `kind`) a `CapabilityRef` cannot carry, and makes Gate 5's recompute-from-`IntentRecord` (F42, §3.4 R3.4.7, §3.9 Gate 5) unconstructible. The named mechanism ("a source test asserting that no member or argument named above is typed `string`") still passes, because none of the three is `string`, so nothing fails open or closed — the defect is a false enumeration on the spine of the authority derivation, not a runtime hole. This is an unclosed dependent of round 2's own repair: round 2 reconciled `requiredConfirmationKind` to F21's list (changing F72 from `(aeKey: string)` to `(ref: CapabilityRef)`) and did not re-check the other two entries against §0.8. §3.2 R3.2.2's non-owning copy omits the function-argument clause entirely, so the two statements of the same source test now differ in scope.
structuralViolations.fix: Scope the sentence to capability-valued arguments — e.g. "every capability-valued argument of …" — or drop `subjectCapability` and `verificationFloor` from the list. Their capability members are already covered: `IntentSubject.capability` and `IntentSubject.handoff_capability_ref` are typed `CapabilityRef | null` by F41, and `FloorSubject` extends `IntentSubject`. Then bring §3.2 R3.2.2 and §A1.7 P-24 into line with the corrected F21 wording.

citations.verdict:
CERTIFIABLE: NO — but narrowly, and for the second round running with zero security-contract violations. Two structural findings, both editorial in consequence, neither touching authority.

WHAT I DID. Read all 6,143 lines of the contract and both repair records. Verified every repository figure by loading the modules and enumerating in process, never by grepping literals.

REPOSITORY, BY EXECUTION — every number exact. ActionCapabilityRegistry.list() = 226; canonicalProductionPolicyDefinitions() = 221 (= 226 minus exactly the 5 kernel.test.* synthetics); MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG = 47; C9_CAPABILITIES = 56. Also confirmed: policyDecision ALLOW 129 / SHADOW_ONLY 95 / DENY 2; ALLOW ∧ authenticated_request = 105; 53 unreachable by source type; MONEY 92 of 226 and 39 of 105 against 12/4 for the bare 'financial' token; BOOKING 13 of which 7 ALLOW; CONSENT 3, IDENTITY 6, MARKETING_FANOUT 4, TENANT_AUTHORITY 28/14; 98 distinct riskFacets tokens; the seven autonomyLevel values at 19/95/1/50/42/14/5; 19 non-test REQUIRED capabilities all resolving approverPolicyKey 'tenant-owner'; 164 of 221 definitions on the permissive twelve-role default; 0 definitions admitting authenticated_request into trustedServiceSourceTypes (F90(3)'s load-bearing exclusion holds); C9 mode 41/13/2 and resourceClass 40/15/1 with c9.no_action the unique LOCAL row (F49's build assertion holds); catalogue riskTier 35/7/3/2 with zero 'restricted' (so F51's no-STEP_UP-for-any-C9-key assertion is satisfiable); TOOL ⊂ C9 with exactly the nine extras F24 names; AE ∩ (C9 ∪ TOOL) = ∅; all 13 F38 pairings resolve on both sides; every key §0.7 F36 says resolves does resolve; the three deleted keys resolve nowhere; all eight NEVER_CHAT_ACTUATED names resolve in no space. F32's polarity case is exact: cash-declaration.declare.execute.v1 is ALLOW, widget-reachable, carries riskFacets ['local','one_target','confirmed_observation','immutable_history'] — no money token — and is caught only by targetKind.

ONE FIGURE IS LOOSE, AND IT IS NOT A FINDING. §0.13 F72 and §2.6.5 BOOK.2 say the deleted chain "routes 118 of 226 capabilities — 94 of the 105 widget-reachable — onto SETTINGS_DRAFT". Executed: 94 of 105 is exact; 118 is the count over the 129 ALLOW, not over 226 — the figure over all 226 is 202. The denominator is wrong; the number is right for the set that matters (only ALLOW is mintable). It falls in none of the three categories, BOOK.2 marks it [NON-NORMATIVE], and it changes no rule, so I have not filed it. Worth one word in an editorial pass.

MUST-HOLD LIST, ITEM BY ITEM.
· Exactly TWO floor reductions, both §0.17 — CONFIRMED. I searched every waive/lower/exempt/relax clause. §2.6.15 SOURCE.3 restates reduction 2's consequence for one intent and creates nothing; F44's ANONYMOUS entries for RISK_FLOOR['read'], EFFECT_FLOOR['CONTROL'] and targetFloor('c') are table design with stated reasons, not reductions from a pinned value; F62/CONSENT.2's escape exclusion narrows a kind-level mint fence, not verificationFloor; K7 and CH1 are ceilings, which lower an effective level, never a floor; §4.8 A-0's append explicitly waives no floor and ranges only over `emitted`. No third clause creates one.
· §2.6.7 CLIENT.2 and §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.3 — CONFIRMED present, unrenumbered, and not superseded. CLIENT.2 is the validateEnvelope refusal of a CLIENT_LIST at presentation_mode 'client'; CLIENT.3 is the distinct bulk-intent role clause. ARTIFACT.3 is the contains_pii clause; ARTIFACT.5 is the distinct fixed-roles clause.
· Gate 5 recomputes verificationFloor from an IntentRecord — CONFIRMED and structurally constructible: FloorSubject = IntentSubject & {effect, priority}, and §3.7's IntentRecord declares capability, handoff_capability_ref, target, effect, priority and widget_kind, so `verificationFloor(record, record.widget_kind)` type-checks and the exempt branch is reproducible.
· Gate 6 dispatches on subjectCapability, and a HANDOFF resolves destination fences only — CONFIRMED. The block binds `const ref = subjectCapability(record); // bound once; NOT record.capability`, guards null first, and the HANDOFF branch states it "NEVER resolves assertCanExecute, c9Capability's domain/mode admission, or the AE commit allowlist."
· Gate 7 re-reads requiredConfirmationKind from the live allowlist for a COMMIT — CONFIRMED, verbatim, naming itself F72's second evaluation point and refusing a key whose row was withdrawn between mint and submission.
· No precedence chain anywhere, Annex A included — CONFIRMED. A0.2 declares none and gives the reason; the one divergence the chain used to adjudicate is folded into §0.21 residual 4.
· No normative clause cites an erratum — CONFIRMED. The only two hits outside Annex B are the preamble's own denial and A1.2.1's remark that the clause it once adjudicated against "was retired with the errata layer".
· Every §N.M citation names a section that carries the rule cited — PARTLY. I checked this exhaustively, not by sampling: I built a clause→section index from the document and machine-checked all 199 citations of the form `§N.M <clause-id>`. All 199 resolve to the declaring section. The thirteen exceptions the checker raised are all in Annex B (which correctly cites the retired numbering) or are table-cell/heading declarations my extractor missed. What survives is five unqualified pointers into sections that are themselves pointers — three normative (§3.3 R3.3.3, §3.9's Gate 6 block, §3.5 R3.5.3, all naming §3.4 for SENSITIVE_DEST or the floor derivation, which §3.4 disclaims in terms) and two in §3.1's shape block. Filed as structural violation 2.
· Every identifier declared exactly once — CONFIRMED. I extracted all 147 top-level `interface`/`type`/`const`/`function`/`declare` names from every fenced block. Exactly one identifier has two sites, and it is the admitted exception: `subjectCapability`'s declare signature at §0.8 F41 line 666 and its one body at §3.5 line 3770. Nothing else.
· The contract's own consolidated-mechanical-audit.mjs: 29/29.

AUTHORITY LENS — mint → emit → submit → gate → canonical. No conferral admitted anywhere. FLOOR_EXEMPT is tight in all four clauses: the effect clause plus §3.2's effect/field table make an actuating intent unconstructible (a REFINE or CONTROL with a null capability is structurally unrepresentable, so the `capability === null` disjunct cannot smuggle one in), and priority is server-set. SENSITIVE_DEST is total over four spaces and fail-closed on an unregistered destination, an unclassified row and a TOOL ref. F72 has no default branch and the fail-closed space guard is redundant-in-fact, because F24's disjointness (verified: AE ∩ (C9 ∪ TOOL) = ∅) means a C9 key can never hit an AE allowlist row. F31's assertion set is satisfiable for the four declared rows — each is ALLOW, reachable from authenticated_request, present in the 221 definitions, and the `ae` side of exactly one F38 pairing; none satisfies MONEY, CONSENT, IDENTITY or TENANT_AUTHORITY; the marketing cardinality is exactly 1. Gate 8-R keys on the record, never on profile_id, and its body_hash echo makes a readback against a superseded body refuse. The one place the general statement and the disclosed exception part company — Gate 6's HANDOFF branch lists targetFloor('s') as a destination fence while F91 waives it for the two FLOOR_EXEMPT class-'s' handoffs — is disclosed and resolved inside §0.17 itself ("the residual fence splits by exemption rather than conjoining terms that never all hold at once"), so it is an exception to a rule, not a contradiction.

F72'S NEW CapabilityRef SIGNATURE BREAKS NO CALLER. Gate 7 passes `subjectCapability(record)`, which is non-null for a COMMIT by §3.2's effect table. §2.6.16 SETTINGS.1 and §2.6.17 FORM.2 index `AE_WIDGET_COMMIT_ALLOWLIST[aeKey]` directly, which is correct — F30 declares that table `Record<string, AeCommitRow>`, string-keyed, and F22's "a CapabilityRef cannot key a Record" applies to the tables keyed on capKey(ref), which this is not. The only residue is cosmetic: §2.6.5 BOOK.2 and §3.10 R3.10.1 both gloss F72's body as "it reads AE_WIDGET_COMMIT_ALLOWLIST[aeKey]" where F72 writes `[ref.key]`. Both sentences say "not restated here" and cite F72, so F72 governs unambiguously and there is nothing to drift into; I have not filed it, but the two glosses should say `ref.key`.

WHAT REMAINS, AND WHY IT STILL BLOCKS. Finding 1 is a false enumeration on the spine of the authority derivation: F21 asserts a typing that §0.8's own declarations of subjectCapability and verificationFloor contradict. It is precisely an unclosed dependent of round 2's F21/F72 reconciliation — round 2 fixed one of the six entries in that list and did not re-check the other five. It fails open on nothing (the mechanism F21 names still passes, because WidgetKind is a literal union, not `string`), but a rule stated falsely about the one function Gate 5 recomputes is not a rule I can certify. Finding 2 is the round-2 class surviving in five places, all of them pointers into pointers, all of them invisible to a resolvability test.

DIRECTION OF TRAVEL, STATED PLAINLY. Round 1: 48 findings, 3 of them security-contract. Round 2: 38, 0 security-contract. This pass: 2, 0 security-contract, 0 unproven normative claims, 0 duplicate declarations beyond the admitted exception, 0 unresolvable references, 0 errata citations, 0 precedence language, exactly 2 floor reductions, all 21 fundamental-rule rows holding, and every one of roughly forty repository figures exact when executed against the live registries. The substance is right and has been right since round 2; what failed here is a typing sentence and five pointers. Both are one-line edits with no dependents to close, and neither requires a fourth adversarial pass — a targeted re-check of those two sites, plus widening the audit script's link test from resolvability to clause-correctness (it already holds the index needed), is sufficient to certify.

This is the round-2 class in its strongest form — a normative clause citing a section that carries nothing — and it defeats F6's own named mechanism, which "fails on a reference that resolves to nothing": as written, the documentation-link test F6 commissions can never go green on this document. The rule itself still stands (buildCellIndex plus the leaf schema carry it), so nothing is unsatisfiable downstream. structuralViolations.clause: §0.18 F93 (line 1561): "**P-12** a step-up mechanism, **P-19** the renderer and CI substrate, **P-23** … **P-32** … Every one is `[ABSENT]` today" — against §A1.5's P-19 row (line 5850), whose Status cell reads `[UNENFORCEABLE-TODAY]`.

One prerequisite row therefore carries two contradictory canonical statements of its status, and F35 additionally requires per-status figures to be "derived from this ledger at build and printed from it, never transcribed into prose" — which is exactly what F93's blanket sentence does. Nothing fails open: A2.1 gives `[ABSENT]` and `[UNENFORCEABLE-TODAY]` identical NORMATIVE-PENDING consequences, so the harm is a drifted status, not a weakened fence.

structuralViolations.clause: §2 K20 (line 2606): "At REGISTRY LOAD, `emittable(kind) = ownerClassKeys(kind) ∩ capabilityRegistry ≠ ∅`" — restated verbatim in §A2.3's enforcement table.
structuralViolations.consequence: `capabilityRegistry` is declared by no shape anywhere in the contract (the three declared lookups are `C9_CAP_BY_KEY`/`c9Registry.tryGet`, `AE_CAP_BY_KEY`/`actionCapabilityRegistry.tryGet` and `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME`), and it names no key space, which §0.6 F21 makes void in a normative sentence — an `OwnerClass` may resolve to C9 keys (`CATALOG_READ`) or AE keys (`ACTION_EXECUTION`), so the right operand is space-ambiguous. This is the derivation that decides whether any of the twenty-two kinds may be emitted at all, and the commit that landed during this pass (dceeb862) declared the formula's other two identifiers — `OwnerClass` and `ownerClassKeys` — for precisely this F2 reason while leaving this one undeclared. Secondary: `ownerClassKeys` is newly declared as `ReadonlySet<CapabilityRef>`, but §0.6 F22 rules that a `CapabilityRef` is an object and that every CapabilityRef-keyed site is keyed on `capKey(ref)`; a set-intersection over ref objects is by identity, not by value, so the derivation is not computable as declared. Fail-closed direction is stated (empty set ⇒ not emittable), so this is under-specification, not a conferral.
structuralViolations.fix: Declare the right operand — e.g. `ownerClassKeys(kind): ReadonlySet<CapabilityRefKey>` and `emittable(kind) = ∃ k ∈ ownerClassKeys(kind) : k ∈ REGISTERED_KEYS`, where `REGISTERED_KEYS` is the space-qualified union of `C9_CAP_BY_KEY`, `AE_CAP_BY_KEY` and `CONTROL_REGISTRY` read through `capKey(ref)`.

structuralViolations.clause: §1.6.7 P10 (line 2196): "`C9_DENIAL_PROJECTION` maps each `c9Deny(...)` code to `{ cell_state, reason_code, limitation_severity }` … *Mechanisms:* (a) an `EP-BUILD` ratchet that enumerates the `c9Deny('…')` literals under `maya-saas-backend/src/orchestration/` — **118 distinct codes**, verified — and fails the build if any code has no row".
structuralViolations.consequence: `C9_DENIAL_PROJECTION` is declared by no shape — not as an interface, not as a `declare const`, not as a normative table with a closed first column. §0.1 F2: "A clause naming an accessor, a member or a catalogue that exists nowhere is not a weaker rule; it is no rule, with the additional harm that it reads as one." The build ratchet P10 commissions tests "any code has no row" in a table whose shape and key form are nowhere fixed. Round 2 set the precedent by declaring `LIMITATION_REASON_TABLE` for this exact reason nine lines above; its sibling table in the same subsection was left undeclared. (The repository half of P10 is exact: I counted the distinct `c9Deny` literals under `src/orchestration/` and got 118.)
structuralViolations.fix: Declare it beside `LIMITATION_REASON_TABLE` in §1.6.7: `interface DenialProjection { cell_state: CellState; reason_code: ReasonCode; limitation_severity: LimitationReason['severity'] }` plus `declare const C9_DENIAL_PROJECTION: Readonly<Record<string, DenialProjection>>`.

structuralViolations.clause: §1.9 H2 (line 2296): "`presentation.text_equivalent = renderTextEquivalent(kind, body, cell_index, intents, locale)`" against §2.3.5 K9 (line 2508): "`renderTextEquivalent(kind, body, intents, locale)` emits exactly `sentence_order` and nothing else".
structuralViolations.consequence: One pure server function, two canonical statements of its input list — arity 5 with `cell_index` and arity 4 without — in two sections, neither marked as a pointer to the other. H2's mechanism is byte-equality recomputation at `EP-MINT` ("the validator recomputes the function and requires byte equality before the hash is taken"), so the input list is load-bearing: an implementer must pick one, and whichever is picked, one of the two normative sentences is false about the function it names. F6a's one-declaration test cannot catch it, because neither statement sits in a fenced block. Lowest-severity of the five: `cell_index` is derivable from `(kind, body_version, body)` through the pure `buildCellIndex`, so the two forms cannot produce different bytes — the defect is a drifted signature, not a divergent output.
structuralViolations.fix: Fix one arity and make the other a citation: keep H2's five-argument form (V1 clause (d) needs the cell index to detect a structural leaf in the text) and have K9 read "`renderTextEquivalent` (§1.9 H2) emits exactly `sentence_order` and nothing else".

wrongSectionCitations: §1.2 V1 mechanism (line 1928) cites «§7's `renderTextEquivalent`» — §7 does not exist; §0.2 F6 fixes five sections and no others. NORMATIVE. Filed as a structural violation.

authority.verdict:
CERTIFIABLE: NO — but by a hair, and not on substance. Round 3: 5 structural, 0 security-contract, 0 unproven. All five are the round-2 class (a citation or a declaration, not a rule), none touches the authority spine, and each is a one-line fix.

FIRST, A FACT ABOUT THE ARTEFACT. The contract changed three times while this pass ran. I read 6,143 lines start to finish at revision 1bf0cf92; then dceeb862 (00:28) declared OwnerClass/ownerClassKeys and trimmed F53, and 71a5be32 (00:31) updated six callers of the retyped requiredConfirmationKind. The file is now 6,178 lines. I re-read every delta as a diff and re-verified all five findings against the current HEAD (71a5be32, tree clean) — they all survive there. No certification can attach to a document that moves under the pass without naming a revision: this one names 71a5be32. That instability is itself worth the owner's attention — the last three commits each repaired a defect and the last one repaired the closure of the one before it.

WHAT HOLDS, ITEM BY ITEM.
• Exactly TWO floor reductions, both in §0.17 F91's table, no third clause creating one. I swept every «floor/lower/waive/reduction» site: §3.4 R3.4.8 and §3.16.8 both point at §0.17 and explicitly refuse to re-enumerate; F44's ANONYMOUS entries (RISK_FLOOR['read'], EFFECT_FLOOR['CONTROL'], targetFloor('c')) are declared table values with their own stated grounds, not reductions from a baseline, and F51 pins the resulting 56-key vector with DELIBERATELY_WITHHELD empty.
• §2.6.7 CLIENT.2 present, unrenumbered, NOT superseded: CLIENT.2 is the validateEnvelope refusal of presentation_mode 'client'; CLIENT.3 is the role:'primary' uniqueness clause — a different subject, and it leaves §2.6.7's pii_ceiling 'client_identified' fence standing. §2.6.22 ARTIFACT.3 likewise: contains_pii, unrenumbered, and ARTIFACT.5 is the fixed-roles clause, not a replacement.
• Gate 5 recomputes verificationFloor from an IntentRecord — literally `verificationFloor(record, record.widget_kind)`, with priority and widget_kind on the record so the FLOOR_EXEMPT branch is reproducible, and any divergence (raised OR lowered) refusing SUPERSEDED / policy_floor_changed.
• Gate 6 dispatches on `subjectCapability(record)` bound once, never record.capability; and for effect === 'HANDOFF' it resolves the DESTINATION fences only — registration in space, SENSITIVE_DEST, targetFloor('s'), the landing surface's own ingress — and explicitly never assertCanExecute, never c9Capability's domain/mode admission, never the AE commit allowlist.
• Gate 7 re-reads requiredConfirmationKind from the live allowlist for a COMMIT, named as F72's second evaluation point, so a row withdrawn between mint and submission refuses.
• No precedence chain anywhere, Annex A included: A0.2 retires it on the ground that the annex and the body speak about different subjects, and nothing else in the document orders two rules. (FR-3's «Gate 14's answer governs any disagreement» is a runtime refusal rule that resolves toward the canonical resolver — not a precedence chain over clauses.)
• No normative clause cites an erratum: zero occurrences of E-n / EB-n / EC-n and zero §0B/§0C references outside Annex B, which is marked [NON-NORMATIVE] and binding on nothing.
• Every identifier declared exactly once, with the one admitted exception. 153 fenced-block declarations; `subjectCapability`'s §0.8 F41 signature + §3.5 body is the admitted pair; `row` is a local binding F6a expressly admits.
• All 21 FR rows hold.
